article.title: Profiling TorchNeuron (Part 1): System-level profiling on AWS Trainium.

harvestedTerms.summary: A technical walkthrough from the Hugging Face blog on profiling ML model inference on AWS Trainium using TorchNeuron, covering three implementations of RMSNorm and demonstrating use of Neuron Explorer and torch.profiler. Highly implementation-focused; limited terminological novelty but touches several longlist terms.

article.title: Why Data Modeling Is Not Enough

harvestedTerms.summary: An MIT Sloan Management Review article arguing that organizations over-invest in data science (prediction, ML) at the expense of decision science (modeling decisions themselves), resulting in high project failure rates. The piece introduces the distinction between data modeling and decision modeling as the key gap to bridge for analytics ROI.

article.title: Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains

harvestedTerms.summary: The Verge reports on new HARC research showing that data center buildout in Texas — driven largely by generative AI demand — could reverse decades of air quality progress, with fine particle pollution potentially tripling and NOx emissions rising 136% within five years depending on energy mix choices. The article frames the data center boom as an acute environmental crisis with modeled outcomes across different energy scenarios.

Brief link-blog post about a serious certificate authority compromise: eight eMudhra intermediate CA private keys were exposed, affecting major root trust stores. Simon Willison flags software updates needed in Python tooling (uv, pip, certifi). The sponsored message mentions AI agent access control as an aside. No substantive AI terminology introduced.

NVIDIA blog primer on AI inference economics covering throughput, latency, goodput, cost-per-token, and the interplay of pretraining/post-training/test-time scaling on inference costs. Primarily educational/marketing content explaining infrastructure economics for enterprise audiences. Introduces 'goodput' as a holistic inference performance metric and frames 'AI factory' as NVIDIA's full-stack inference platform concept.

article.title: Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains

harvestedTerms.summary: A Verge article reporting on new HARC research quantifying how data center expansion in Texas could reverse decades of air quality gains, with NOx emissions potentially rising 136% and fine particle pollution more than tripling. The piece is primarily environmental reporting on the physical-infrastructure consequences of the AI buildout, with data on gas turbine use, onsite power generation, and pollution modelling scenarios.

Simon Willison reports on the compromise of private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates, which chain to roots trusted by major browser and OS root programs. The post notes downstream impact on Python tooling (pip, uv, certifi) and Linux ca-certificates packages.

An NVIDIA blog post explaining the economics of AI inference, covering key metrics (tokens, throughput, latency, goodput), scaling law types (pretraining, post-training, test-time), and the role of full-stack hardware/software codesign in reducing cost per token. Primarily a vendor explainer with some useful conceptual framing around 'goodput' as a holistic performance metric.
